entries: {@i Demon of Assassination}

Abvekus are demons that embody assassins' sadistic professionalism. Patient killers, they prefer to stalk targets from afar before striking. These targets might be the abvekus' enemies or the enemies of demon lords or powerful villains the abvekus serve.

Abvekus are bipedal, insectile demons whose arms end in scythe-like claws. They take pride in their kills and sometimes wear or otherwise display grisly trophies taken from the bodies of their victims.
{@i Demon of Destruction and Sieges}
Rendeliths are hulking demons that lead armies in destroying enemy castles, strongholds, and other fortifications. They delight in toppling defenses so demonic hordes can rush into the fray.

Rendeliths have the upper bodies of humanoids but the lower bodies of oxen, with stony spikes along their backs. These cruel demons are masters of strategy that delight in magically producing walls and ditches to drive enemy armies into ambushes. Such ambushes often involve hordes of armanites—similar-looking but weaker demons driven by unrestrained bloodlust.

Most rendeliths have fought for so long in the Blood War, a raging conflict between demons and devils, that they think only in terms of combat. Each wall they collapse brings them grim satisfaction, but their unquenchable drive for the next battle pushes them ever onward.
{@i Wicked Serpentine Oppressors}

Powerful and magical, sarrukhs once commanded a wicked empire that spanned Faerûn, but it fell tens of thousands of years ago. In the millennia that followed, the many species sarrukhs created drove them nearly to extinction. Only a small number of sarrukhs remain in isolated enclaves, including a small community beneath the Citadel at the heart of Thaymount.

Sarrukhs have snakelike lower bodies and heads but torsos that resemble those of humanoids. Their gleaming eyes are alight with inner fire. Sarrukhs can live for up to a millennium, and most expect to see their empire rise again.

entries.name: Sarrukh Tyrant
entries: Most remaining sarrukhs are tyrants who fervently believe the sarrukh empire's resurgence is inevitable. Tyrants live in clans with other sarrukhs, roaming ruins and subjugating creatures that live nearby. They command only a small portion of the magical power their former empire's leaders held.

entries.name: Arisen Sarrukh
entries: The most powerful sarrukhs are arisen: horrific creatures that have subverted death. While arisen sarrukhs have lost their ability to cast spells, their unliving flesh is unnaturally strong.

images.title: An arisen sarrukh commands two sarrukh tyrants.

entries: Once the undisputed regent of Thay, Szass Tam is an old and powerful lich who plots to regain control over the nation. Although he still wields great power as the zulkir of necromancy and the tharchion of Thaymount (see chapter 1), Szass Tam believes it's his destiny to rule Thay and use its living people as fodder for his undead armies.

entries.name: History
entries: An eloquent and inventive wizard, Szass Tam rose through the ranks of the Red Wizards to become the zulkir of necromancy more than three centuries ago and became a lich not long afterward.

entries.name: Regency
entries: Over a century ago, Szass Tam turned against the other zulkirs and claimed rulership over Thay. On winning the ensuing civil war, he declared himself regent and turned his rivals into undead servants. Under his rule, necromancers dominated Thay, and all paid fealty to him.

entries.name: Pursuit of Godhood
entries: Eventually Szass Tam craved more than ruling Thay. Obsessed with gaining more power, he began a ritual to ascend to godhood. When this ritual failed spectacularly a few decades ago, civil unrest in Thay prompted him to reestablish the zulkir council with members loyal to him. He relinquished his title of regent, though in reality, the new zulkirs reported to him. These zulkirs dealt with the details of government, leaving him free to pursue new approaches to attaining godhood.

While Szass Tam remained distracted with finding a different way to attain godhood, new rivals systematically overthrew his sycophant zulkirs. Suddenly he was again part of a zulkir council with Red Wizards who saw themselves as his equals and refused to bow to him as the nation's ruler.

entries.name: Returning Tyrant
entries: While Szass Tam still aspires to godhood, he can't bear the loss of political power to rivals he views as inferiors. After years of plotting, he again moves to subdue Thay with undead before crushing the zulkirs who oppose him. If successful, he'll return Thay to the undead-dominated land it was under his rule.

entries.name: Personality
entries: Szass Tam takes the long view in his many plots, some of which span lifetimes. He is quick to pivot to contingencies when necessary.

While he enjoys commanding fear in his Thayan subjects, he also wields diplomacy to maintain foreign allies and is skilled at keeping foes off balance. Those who cross Szass Tam might evoke one of his legendary rages or might earn a nod of appreciation, as of someone witnessing a clever move in a game of strategy.

entries.name: Szass Tam's Lair
entries: Szass Tam's lair is the Citadel, a fortress in the mountainous region of Thaymount. Here he plans his evil schemes and issues commands to his underlings.

Xelnene Thrul is the zulkir of evocation. With the exception of Szass Tam, she is the most powerful mage on the Council of Zulkirs. She hates tyranny and wants Szass Tam destroyed. To her, the only good tyrant is a dead one.

entries.name: History
entries: Xelnene Thrul is the scion of a powerful family. Her ancestor, Aznar Thrul, was zulkir of evocation a century ago. He murdered countless Thayans and conscripted vast armies in failed attempts to conquer Rashemen. Xelnene hates Aznar's deeds but trades on her family's fearsome reputation when needed.

As a youth, Thrul was apprenticed to a Red Wizard named Sabeine who cultivated Thrul's sense of justice and encouraged Thrul to foster goodness among the Red Wizards. Szass Tam later executed Sabeine for treason. Ever since, Thrul has kept her desire for reform secret.

entries.name: Personality
entries: Thrul is shrewd and pragmatic. She exudes physical, political, and magical might but avoids showing emotion lest her enemies find her weak. She commands a network of spies, allies, and political operatives who advance her goal of creating a better future for Thay's populace.
